TCP slow start is the initial congestion control phase where the congestion window (cwnd) grows quickly during each round-trip time (RTT). This phase allows the sender to gradually increase the amount of data it sends into the network, checking for signs of congestion through packet loss and adjusting the sending rate accordingly.

**Example:**

Imagine a sender starts with a congestion window (cwnd) size of 10 segments. During the first RTT, the sender transmits all 10 segments and waits for acknowledgment (ACK). If no packet loss is detected, the cwnd is increased to 20 segments for the next RTT. This doubling continues until congestion is detected, at which point the cwnd will be reduced due to packet loss, and a new slow start phase will begin.
